must_fix.title: Combobox: Enter selects an option that became disabled while it was active
must_fix.evidence: src/Combobox.tsx looks up activeEntry in `visible`, which includes disabled options, and the Enter branch calls commit(activeEntry.option) without checking disabled; handleChange also keeps a disabled active option. Probe: render options [Apple, Banana], click, ArrowDown (Apple active), rerender with Apple disabled:true, press Enter -> output `active after disable «r0»-option-0` and `A onChange [ [ 'a' ] ]`. The issue requires disabled options to be skipped, and the README says disabled options can't be selected. No test covers this.

nits: The 'No results' role="status" live region is added at the same moment as its text, so screen readers may not announce it. Keeping an always-present empty status element would fix that.
Dialog's TABBABLE selector leaves out contenteditable, summary and iframe, and it treats each radio in a group as a separate Tab stop.
Dialog uses a truthiness check for `description`, so description={0} renders nothing and drops aria-describedby.

report:
I'd hold this PR for one bug. `pnpm test` passes (86 tests in 5 files) and `pnpm typecheck` is clean, with no warnings in the test output. The README matches the code, and I found no unrelated edits or leftover files.

**Must fix: Combobox lets Enter select a disabled option.** If the parent marks the active option as disabled while the listbox is open, it stays active and Enter selects it. The issue says disabled options are skipped and can't be selected. The cause is in `src/Combobox.tsx`:
- `activeEntry` is looked up in `visible`, which still includes disabled options.
- The Enter branch calls `commit(activeEntry.option)` without checking `disabled`.
- `handleChange` also keeps `active` whenever the option is still visible, even if it's disabled.

I reproduced it with a probe test, since removed:
```tsx
const opts = [{ value: 'a', label: 'Apple' }, { value: 'b', label: 'Banana' }];
const { rerender } = render(<Combobox label="F" options={opts} value={null} onChange={onChange} />);
await user.click(combobox); await user.keyboard('{ArrowDown}');
rerender(<Combobox label="F" options={[{ ...opts[0], disabled: true }, opts[1]]} value={null} onChange={onChange} />);
await user.keyboard('{Enter}');
```
Output:
```
active after disable «r0»-option-0
A onChange [ [ 'a' ] ]
```
The fix is to work out the active option from enabled options only, and to add a test for this case.

Edge cases I tried that behave correctly:
- Tab values whose ids could collide (`"a b"` and `"a%20b"`) get distinct ids.
- Dialog under `StrictMode` moves focus inside on open, closes on Escape and returns focus to the opener.
- Tabs under `StrictMode` skips the disabled tab when moving with the arrow keys.
- A Combobox inside a Dialog: clicking an option doesn't close the dialog.

`git status` is the same as when I started.
